Rationale.GT1_ModelGeneralization: Concept and token induction heads were successfully identified across 6 different models from different model families (Llama-2-7b, Meta-Llama-3-8B, Pythia-6.9b, OLMo-2-1124-7B, OLMo-2-0425-1B, Llama-3.2-3B). The causal scores methodology transferred successfully to new architectures (Pythia/GPT-NeoX style, OLMo), demonstrating the induction head identification generalizes beyond the original Llama-2-7b model.
Rationale.GT2_DataGeneralization: The findings were validated on extensive new data: (1) The FVS country-capital dataset contains 175 NEW country-capital pairs not in the word2vec dataset, achieving 54.9% accuracy with concept lens. (2) Combined testing across 75,825 examples from two independent datasets (word2vec: 42,306, FVS: 33,519) showed consistent patterns where concept lens outperforms on semantic tasks and token lens outperforms on morphological tasks.
Rationale.GT3_MethodGeneralization: The concept/token lens methodology was successfully applied to 43 different task types spanning semantic tasks (28), morphological tasks (12), and other tasks (3). The method shows consistent patterns across all categories: concept lens excels at semantic tasks (capital-countries: 89.5% vs 15.8% raw) while token lens excels at morphological tasks (plural: 58.9% vs 35.5% concept). This demonstrates the method generalizes across different relationship types, datasets, and task complexities.
